body:
integer division by zero getting a FP exception is something we cannot avoid, it's a hardware exception. Numpy wraps it's integer division code to literally check the denominators with conditionals and instead generates fpectl exceptions. I dont think this can be a hi-pri issue for us just looking at the amount of work involved in refactoring TH.

Your second issue looks more like a bug.
The first one is expected, second one is a bug in printing, when there are no non NaN and inf values in the tensor.
the printing is fixed now in master via https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/332

issue.body:
```python
import torch

torch.autograd.Variable(torch.LongTensor([18])) / 0.0625
# Floating point exception (core dumped)

torch.LongTensor([18]) / 0.0625
#Traceback (most recent call last):
#  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
#  File ".../lib/python2.7/site-packages/torch/tensor.py", line 294, in __div__
#    return self.div(other)
#TypeError: div received an invalid combination of arguments - got (float), but expected one of:
# * (int value)
#      didn't match because some of the arguments have invalid types: (float)
# * (torch.LongTensor other)
#      didn't match because some of the arguments have invalid types: (float)
```
at `0.4.0a0+b608ea9`;  related to https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/327 and maybe https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/5411 

Probably the cause is that in the variable case, it casts the divisor as Long and it triggers integer division by zero. But why only in the variable case?

Didn't test it after the tensor+variable merge, since don't want to migrate to vNext before ECCV deadline :)

body:
I'm re-opening this issue because it has appeared plenty of times in the past (see linked issues, plus many others that haven't been linked).

From discussion in https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/8079, both TensorFlow and numpy handles the 0 / 0 division gracefully, so the performance hit of adding an extra check (for integer tensors) wouldn't be that bad in comparison.

With the current implementation, adding those checks only amounts to a few extra lines, so I think it should be reconsidered.

rename.from: Segmentation fault when divising by zero with integer tensors
rename.to: Segmentation fault when dividing by zero with integer tensors

body:
Here is what I propose that we do for now.

We only handle the division case explicitly for now.

Other operators which might internally have a division by zero (like `log(0)`) can be handled later. As an example, `log(0)` does not segfault currently because `log` is not implemented for integer types in PyTorch for now.

Instead of following an approach similar to `numpy`, [where the integer and floating point cases are handled similarly](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/blob/31ffdecf07d18ed4dbb66b171cb0f998d4b190fa/numpy/core/src/umath/loops.c.src#L1009-L1011), we instead only add the runtime checks for integer types, [as is BTW what numpy has in a FIXME note](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/blob/31ffdecf07d18ed4dbb66b171cb0f998d4b190fa/numpy/core/src/umath/loops.c.src#L1003-L1008).

## What it looks like

### For the CPU case:

modify https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/caed485873a750fa698c402e7d64f9b1c386cca9/aten/src/ATen/native/cpu/BinaryOpsKernel.cpp#L71-L78 to also check if `b` is zero, in which case we set a  flag in the loop indicating that a `ZeroDivisionError` should be raised

### For the GPU case:

add an `assert` in the lambda if the divisor is zero for integer types. This is not consistent with CPU (which raises a `ZeroDivisionError`), but is the same as what we do for advanced indexing for now, see
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/caed485873a750fa698c402e7d64f9b1c386cca9/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/IndexKernel.cu#L60 
Once https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/16960 gets merged, we can revisit the assert with something else.

cc @gchanan for thoughts
